summary: Alberta lookout in our records; no public source found names this tower or describes its build date, staffing or current use.

evidence.supports: Alberta publishes a map of its 127 wildfire lookout sites, across the boreal forest and along the Rocky Mountains
evidence.quote: Map showing the locations of Alberta's 127 wildfire lookout sites, which are situated throughout the province's boreal forest and along the Rocky Mountains.

evidence.supports: each site is staffed by an observer, generally from April to October, who watches for wildfire all day
evidence.quote: Each site is staffed by a lookout observer whose job is to watch for wildfire all day, each day, generally from April to October.

evidence.supports: lookout sites are isolated and staff must prepare for a range of possibilities, including meeting a curious bear
evidence.quote: Wildfire lookout sites are isolated and the staff that work them must be prepared for a wide range of possibilities, including an encounter with a curious bear.

notes_for_editor: NO SITE SOURCE: searches and cached-page checks found nothing public about the Meridian lookout by name (no history, build date, height, staffing or current use). The record's build year (2005), height (30 m), elevation (940 m) and access (closed) come from the Alberta Wildfire lookout data (friaa_firesmart_vector_data layer) and are not in any public source I found, so they are left out. The Gift Lake research recorded that Alberta Wildfire's lookout layer is marked protected; I did not check this layer's status, so check before publishing any value taken from it. A 2009 Alberta lookout map in the cache (data/raw/expansion/prairies-north/ab_lookout_map_2009.txt) appears to label MERIDIAN, but no public URL is recorded for it, so it is not cited. The story is general Alberta context plus an honest gap; consider holding it until a site-specific source turns up.
